    How this was made

    Collection. arXiv: every preprint whose title or abstract contains the phrase "causal inference" (3,850 papers). OpenAlex: the 2,000 most-cited journal articles, books and preprints matching the same phrase, minus duplicates of arXiv papers and records without abstracts (1,777 kept). Both searched October 24, 2026. Text features. Each paper is represented by its title (weighted double) plus the six most distinctive terms of its abstract, chosen by TF-IDF across the whole set, with two-word phrases such as "propensity score" kept intact. Clustering and labels. Non-negative matrix factorization found 22 topics; one with fewer than 60 papers was folded into each paper's next-best topic. Labels and descriptions were written by reading each topic's top terms and its most central and most cited papers, then grouped into three families by similarity (named at the end of each topic description). Map layout. Positions come from UMAP over three views of each paper: its topic mix, a latent-semantic projection of the terms, and word-vector meaning (spaCy's large English vectors). Nearby dots discuss similar things; distance between far-apart islands is only roughly meaningful. This page uses the same data as the earlier version of this atlas in the common format of the other maps; it has no paper summaries, and OpenAlex entries show their citation count instead. Papers by Yuta Kawakami that the searches above did not pick up were added by hand on request afterwards; each was placed in its closest topic and next to the most similar titles on the map.
